title: comfy workflow *
description: Output shape for workflow editing commands (slots, set-slot, vary) and the read-only notes reader.

nodes.description: ls-nodes: an ARRAY with one row per TOP-LEVEL node — a subgraph instance is a single opaque row here, and `count` is the length of that array. Deliberately carries no `type` keyword: this schema is shared by the whole `workflow` command group, and `compose`/`decompose` reuse the `nodes` key for an INTEGER node count. The `items` subschema below therefore constrains only the array form.

id.description: node id as serialized in the workflow

type.description: class_type as serialized in the workflow; a string (or absent/null) in any well-formed file. Copied verbatim rather than coerced, so a hand-edited or corrupt file is reported as it actually is.

title.description: display title, else the `Node name for S&R` property; same verbatim-copy caveat as `type`

mode.description: present ONLY when the node is disabled (litegraph mode 2/4); absent for a normally-executing node

subgraph_nodes.description: ls-nodes: one row per node INSIDE a live subgraph instance (definitions.subgraphs[].nodes, recursively) — nodes that never appear in `nodes`. Empty when the workflow has no subgraph instances. This listing INCLUDES disabled nodes: a row's own `mode` says whether it is muted/bypassed, and because a nested instance gets a row of its own, a caller deciding what actually EXECUTES must also check the `mode` of every ancestor along the row's `path` prefixes (a live `10/3/7` under a muted `10/3` is dropped by workflow_to_api, as is any interior under a disabled top-level instance — whose mode is on its `nodes[]` row).

path.description: `<instance>/<interior>` address, nesting with `/` (e.g. "10/3/7") — the same addressing `comfy workflow slots` uses, so it composes into a slot address

instance.description: id of the TOP-LEVEL subgraph instance this row is reached through

id.description: interior node id as serialized in the subgraph definition

type.description: class_type as serialized in the definition; same verbatim-copy caveat as the `nodes[]` `type`

title.description: display title, else the `Node name for S&R` property; same verbatim-copy caveat as `type`

mode.description: present ONLY when the interior node is disabled; workflow_to_api drops such a node after expansion, so nothing else reveals it

subgraph_count.description: ls-nodes: length of `subgraph_nodes` (kept separate from `count`, which stays top-level-only).

subgraph_truncated.description: ls-nodes: present and true ONLY when the interior walk hit its row ceiling, so `subgraph_nodes` is INCOMPLETE and `subgraph_count` is a floor rather than a total. Any listing whose reachable interior rows exceed the ceiling sets it — usually a branching definition graph, which can expand a few-KB file into billions of rows, but a legitimately huge workflow reaches it the same way. Ordinary workflows are far below the ceiling and never carry this key.

notes.description: notes: the Note/MarkdownNote documentation nodes the workflow carries, in graph order (top-level nodes first, then each subgraph definition).

id.description: node id as serialized in the workflow

title.description: author-set node title; null when the node uses its default title

text.description: the note body (widgets_values[0]); empty string when the node carries no usable text

pos.description: canvas position, passed through verbatim — litegraph has serialized this as both [x, y] and {"0": x, "1": y}; null when absent

size.description: canvas size, passed through verbatim (same shape caveat as pos); null when absent

subgraph.description: null for a top-level note; {id, name} of the owning subgraph definition otherwise

source.description: print: the rendered Python-like source, one line per node.

bindings.description: print: binding name -> node id. Interior subgraph nodes use qualified keys/ids, e.g. "10/3/primitive_int" -> "10/3/6".

node_count.description: print: nodes that got a rendered line (top level + subgraph interiors). null for `comfy workflow get` on a non-JSON body.

skipped.description: print: nodes not rendered as their own line. UI-only splicing nodes (reason "spliced", or "inlined into <id>.<input>" for a PrimitiveNode); notes, which are rendered as `#`-comments in `source` AND listed here with reason "note".

wrote.description: file written, or null when nothing was written (set-slot --stdout)

out.description: set-slot: where the result went — "stdout" when --stdout returned it instead of writing the file

workflow_json.description: set-slot --stdout: the modified workflow itself (human mode prints it raw on stdout instead)

variants.description: vary without --out-dir: the produced workflows (human mode prints them as NDJSON on stdout instead); null when they were written to --out-dir

item_map.description: compose: foreach item -> provenance map. Mirrors the `_meta.items` block embedded in each written workflow (`_meta.schema == "compose/1"`).

nodes.description: node ids this item's branch produced (numerically sorted, includes the save node)

save_node.description: auto-appended save node id, null when the branch is terminal
